1. Introduction to Machine Learning (ML)
Machine Learning (ML) is a subfield of artificial intelligence (AI) that focuses on building systems
capable of learning from data, identifying patterns, and making decisions with minimal human
intervention. Unlike traditional programming, where explicit rules are coded to solve a

Machine Learning is broadly categorized into three main types:
1. Supervised Learning: The algorithm is trained on a labeled dataset, meaning the input data is
paired with the correct output. The model learns the mapping function from inputs to outputs.

4. Regularization
When training machine learning models, a common problem is overfitting. Overfitting occurs when a
model learns the training data too well, capturing the noise and random fluctuations rather than the
underlying pattern. An overfitted model performs exceptionally well on the training data but

attern. An overfitted model performs exceptionally well on the training data but poorly on
new, unseen data.
Regularization is a set of techniques used to prevent overfitting by discouraging the model from
becoming too complex. It achieves this by adding a "penalty" term to the loss function that the model
is trying to minimize.
The total loss function becomes the standard error (the difference

to minimize.
The total loss function becomes the standard error (the difference between the model's predictions
and actual data) plus a penalty for model complexity. A hyperparameter (often referred to as lambda)
controls the strength of the regularization. A higher value means more regularization, leading to a
simpler model.

Types of Regularization in Regression
The two most common types of regularization applied to regression models are Ridge Regression (L2)
and Lasso Regression (L1).
4.1. Ridge Regression (L2 Regularization)
Ridge regression adds a penalty term proportional to the square of the magnitude of the
coefficients.
Effect: It shrinks the coefficients of less important features close to zero,

Effect: It shrinks the coefficients of less important features close to zero, but it rarely forces
them exactly to zero. This helps in reducing model complexity and handling multicollinearity
(when independent variables are highly correlated).

Summary of Regularization
Regularization is crucial for building models that generalize well to new data. By applying L1 or L2
regularization, data scientists can control the complexity of Linear and Logistic regression models,
ensuring they remain robust and reliable.
